_readme: NOMOS-SPEC-007 rev. 1.10 §5.3a: verifying a revocation source. For each case, apply §5.3a to `list` with `root_public_key_pem`, `own_certs` and `now`, and compare with `expected` field for field (revoked_kids and revoked_certs sorted). Expectations are written by hand. Keys come from published seeds: never trust material.

cases.name: key_revocation_ed25519
cases.description: An intermediate revokes a key it certified. The list carries both certificates and is signed by the root: the key is revoked and the list is current as of generated_at.

cases.name: key_revocation_es256
cases.description: A P-256 intermediate, as held in a KMS, revokes a key with an ES256 statement (1.10 §5.1). Under 1.9 it could certify the key but never revoke it.

cases.name: certificate_revocation
cases.description: The root withdraws one certificate it issued, by fingerprint. Only that delegation is revoked; the key itself is not.

cases.name: forged_parent_ignored
cases.description: A key the root never certified signs a certificate for K (K's public key is public) and then revokes K. Under 1.7.0 §5.1 that counted; under 1.10 the signer is not recognized and the statement is ignored.

cases.name: parent_certificate_missing
cases.description: The intermediate revokes K, but no certificate INT→K is available. The statement cannot be checked, so it is ignored, never trusted.

cases.name: certificate_not_signed_by_the_parent
cases.description: The intermediate is recognized and signs the statement, but the certificate INT→K it relies on was not signed by the intermediate. Without a certificate the parent really made, it has no standing over K (§5.1a rule 4).

cases.name: statement_signature_invalid
cases.description: A statement altered after it was signed.

cases.name: fingerprint_in_revoked_kid
cases.description: The pre-1.10 reference platform signed certificate revocations with the fingerprint in revoked_kid. Read as 1.10 requires, that is a key revocation of a kid no certificate names, so it revokes nothing. It must be re-signed as revoked_fingerprint.

cases.name: both_targets_malformed
cases.description: A statement naming a key and a certificate is malformed: exactly one is allowed.

cases.name: statement_from_the_future
cases.description: A statement issued after the relying party's clock is malformed.

cases.name: passkey_cannot_revoke
cases.description: A passkey may sign consents and nothing else (rev. 1.9 §3.6). It signs a certificate and an ES256 revocation anyway: its scope does not permit ES256, so it is not recognized as a signer.

cases.name: revoked_parent_still_counts
cases.description: The intermediate revoked K, and was later revoked by the root itself. Revocations accumulate (§5.1a): K stays revoked. If a revoked parent's statements stopped counting, K would come back to life on its other path (root→K).

cases.name: statements_reordered
cases.description: The previous case with its statements and certificates in reverse order: the same result.

cases.name: list_signer_outside_the_hierarchy
cases.description: A hosting platform's own key signs the list. Its statements count on their own authority, but the root does not reach the platform key, so the list establishes no as_of.

cases.name: list_signature_invalid
cases.description: The list's date was changed after signing. Its statements still count; it establishes no as_of.

cases.name: list_signer_revoked
cases.description: A list signer certified by the root, revoked by a statement in this very list. The statement counts; a revoked key cannot vouch that the list is current, so there is no as_of.

cases.name: list_signer_certified
cases.description: The same list signer, unrevoked: the list is current as of generated_at.

cases.name: own_certificates_supply_the_parent
cases.description: The list carries no certificates. The relying party's own (from the issuer document, say) supply the path.

cases.name: list_from_the_future
cases.description: A list dated after the relying party's clock establishes no as_of; its statements still count.

cases.name: parent_certificate_expired_since
cases.description: The intermediate's certificate expired in September. A statement it signed in June still counts: the parent is checked at issued_at. One it signed in October, after expiry, does not.

cases.name: wrong_suite_statement
cases.description: An Ed25519 parent's statement labelled ES256: the key type fixes the suite, so the signature does not verify.

cases.name: malformed_list
cases.description: statements is not an array: the list is MALFORMED and contributes nothing.
